description.value: A first-person account of a long dormancy, told at the mouth chamber in the days after a waking, when such accounts are heard and at no other time. The form is recognised: it must be told standing, and it must include what the teller was wrong about.

content.value:
I was at the mouth and the plug was out and the wind was in the gallery, and I was not cold. That is the part I was wrong about.

Somebody knocked from outside, two and a pause and one, and I went and cut the plug, and it was me coming in. I let myself past and went back to the chamber, and the one who had come in stayed at the mouth and kept the count, and did it better than I have.

When I woke I knocked third. I had expected to knock first. The one who knocked first was in the store all four years and had nothing to do with any of it.
